chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The grape juice, when it is cooked until two-thirds of it evaporates and there remains a third of it, so it is Permissible'.

key_terms.الْعَصِيرُ: Grape juice (specifically from grapes, often used in discussions of khamr)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on grape juice that has been boiled until two-thirds evaporates?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between raw grape juice and 'Tala’a' (concentrated syrup), establishing that boiling off two-thirds of the volume renders the remaining third permissible even if it retains some intoxicating potential. This ruling is pivotal in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between a non-intoxicating foodstuff and khamr, reflecting the principle that concentration alone does not equate to intoxication unless it reaches a specific threshold. The narration underscores the practical application of the 'minority of water' rule in determining the status of grape derivatives.
